Without this, even a 'clean' event-level halt may hide state divergence, so resumption must be refused.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The system has no checkpointing mechanism, making every halt a potential state-divergence risk.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checkpoint was written but not fsynced before exhaustion.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checkpoint and log tail were written non-atomically, so one may persist without the other.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The system's state is fully derivable from the event log alone (event sourcing), which would make this condition unnecessary.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The event log records discrete events, but the system's working state may include intermediate computation not yet materialized as an event. An atomic checkpoint guarantees state and event-log-tail are consistent. If the halt occurred between checkpoints, reconstructing state from the log tail may produce a different state than the runtime actually held, causing resumed events to diverge, duplicate, or skip\u2014corrupting append-only identity through causal gaps or collisions.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
